name: Pre-workout / stim stacks

lead: Pre-workouts are stimulant-heavy supplements taken before training, mostly built on caffeine.
Caffeine has research support for focus and endurance, while evidence for many other ingredients is mixed.

paras: Caffeine blocks adenosine receptors, reducing perceived fatigue and pain; other ingredients target blood flow and muscle buffering.
Reported risks include raised blood pressure, nausea, contamination and undeclared banned substances. The FDA has limited pre-market oversight of supplements.

lead: Pre-workout supplements are products taken before training to boost energy, focus and endurance, usually containing caffeine along with ingredients such as beta-alanine, citrulline and creatine.[1] They are sold as powders, capsules and drinks, often as proprietary blends, and the category is lightly regulated.[1]

Caffeine is reported to improve focus and endurance, but effects of many other ingredients are described as mixed or weak, and commercial doses are often below those studied.[1] Safety concerns include blood pressure effects, contaminated products and undeclared banned substances.[1]
infobox: Caffeine (about 86% of top sellers in one study)[1]

paras: Dan Duchaine formulated Ultimate Orange in 1982, described as the first pre-workout.[1] Ephedrine was banned in US supplements in 2004, and DMAA-containing products such as Jack3d were later targeted by the FDA, with substitutes like DMBA appearing afterward.[1]
Caffeine acts as an adenosine receptor antagonist and is linked to better focus and reduced reaction time.[1] Evidence for carbohydrates, BCAAs, arginine and several plant extracts is mixed.[1]

Reported effects include nausea and skin tingling from beta-alanine, and higher blood pressure from caffeine.[1] Up to half of some blends were found contaminated with melamine in one study, and undeclared SARMs and prohormones have caused failed drug tests.[1]
Trials exist on individual ingredients such as caffeine and creatine, with results summarised above.[1] No studies found on "high caffeine stim stacks" as a combined appearance intervention.
